edges.rationale: Synthetic data generation is explicitly used to increase training data quality when human-generated data is limited or lower quality, so understanding data quality criteria is needed to evaluate and target synthetic data improvements.
Synthetic data generation is used to increase training data quantity, so understanding quantity requirements and cost trade-offs is needed to determine how much synthetic data to produce.

Phase-specific data mixes define domain composition across training phases, which requires understanding data coverage criteria to ensure the right mix of domains and topics without over- or under-representation.

Phase-specific data mixes involve volume considerations across training phases, so understanding data quantity criteria is needed to balance data amounts against training costs and desired capabilities per phase.
